newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK APRIL INFLATION BETWEEN 5.8-5.9PCT - ECON OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: GREEK APRIL INFLATION BETWEEN 5.8-5.9PCT - ECON OFFICIAL.

text.p: Greece's consumer price inflation will fall to 5.8 or 5.9 percent year-on-year in April from 6.0 percent in March, the chairman of the council of economic advisors at the national economy ministry Yannis Stournaras told Reuters.
"Inflation will fall to 5.8 percent or 5.9 percent in April," said Stournaras. "It is a matter of decimals but it seems to be tilting more towards the 5.9 percent right now."
National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou told reporters on Tuesday that inflation dropped below 6.0 percent in April.
"Inflation fell below 6.0 percent in April," said Papandoniou after meeting with Prime Minister Costas Simitis today to discuss the economy.
The April CPI-based inflation figure will be released on Thursday, an official at the National Statistics Service (NSS) told Reuters on Monday.

The central government budget deficit stood at 850 billion drachmas in the first four months of this year which is lower than the 1.2 trillion drachma deficit registered in the same period in 1996 measured on a cash basis, said Stournaras.
The 1997 central government budget deficit was initally projected at 6.2 percent of GDP but has been revised upwards to 7.2 percent of GDP measured on administrative basis.

The central government budget deficit was initially projected at 8.4 percent of GDP in 1996 but has been revised upwards to 9.3 percent in November 1996 and 9.7 percent in 1997 measured on an administrative basis.
Figures derived from an administrative basis accounting system are not comparable with those from a cash basis system.

The general government budget deficit -- the Maastricht fiscal criterion-- is forecast at 4.2 percent of GDP in 1997 from a provisional 7.4 percent of GDP in 1996 measured on a national accounts basis.

The 1996 trade deficit appears to be lower by 350 billion drachmas according to NSS figures that include drachma-denominated exports to the Balkans and other Eastern European countries, said Stournaras.
Papandoniou said the balance of payments could end up being better than central bank figures indicated according to NSS trade data.
The trade deficit widened to 4.44 trillion drachmas ($18.36 billion) in 1996 from 3.99 trillion drachmas ($17.14 billion) in 1995 according to central bank figures.
Bank of Greece is expected to overhaul its balance of payments compilation system this year to incorporate drachma-denominated exports and imports.
"The amount of 350 billion drachmas accounts for more than 1.0 percent of GDP," said the chairman of economic advisors.
The exact positive impact of the smaller trade deficit in 1996 on real GDP growth has yet to be estimated, added Stournaras.
Real 1997 GDP growth was initially put at 3.3 percent but has been revised upward to 3.5 percent from a provisional 2.6 percent in 1996.
GDP is provisionally set at 29.576 trillion drachmas in 1996 and is projected at 32.643 trillion in 1997, based on current prices.
